|
| **Disposition:** needs test
| **From:** FR-136
|
| **Written:** 2026-10-24
|
| **Steps**
|
| 1. Before you start, File > Backup TrainControl Data.  Have a layout with an autonomy setup loaded, at least one train placed, and power on.  Open the autonomy editor: Autonomy > Edit Autonomy on Page, pick a page, choose `Autonomy Setup` in the sidebar.  Leave it open.  In the main window, on the Auto tab, press `Start Autonomous Operation`.  Then open the `Timetable` page of that tab and press `Execute Timetable`.  Then press `Return Home`.  Then, back on the first page of that tab, double-click one of the paths in a train's list of available paths.
| 2. Close the autonomy editor with `Cancel`.  On the Track Diagram tab press `Edit`, pick a page, and leave that editor open.  In the main window press `Start Autonomous Operation` and double-click a path on a train's card on the Auto tab again.  Close the track editor with `Cancel` and answer Yes to "Are you sure you want to close the editor without saving changes?"
| 3. Pick a route that takes a while to run (for instance one with a delay of ten seconds or more) and run it from the Routes tab.  While it is running press `Start Autonomous Operation`, `Execute Timetable`, `Return Home`, and double-click a path on the Auto tab.
| 4. While that route is still running, open Locomotives > Browse Database, right-click a locomotive the route drives and choose `Edit Name/Address/Decoder`, then right-click it again and choose `Delete from Database`.  Then open Layouts > Open Layout... and Layouts > Create New Layout.  Close any window that opens and let the route finish.
| 5. Press `Power OFF`.  Press `Start Autonomous Operation`, `Execute Timetable` and `Return Home`, and double-click a path on the Auto tab.  Then press `ON`.
| 6. Make the setup unusable: in the autonomy editor right-click one end of a link between two pages and choose `Unpair This Link`, then press `Save Changes`.  (If your layout has no links, skip steps 6 and 7.)  In the main window press `Start Autonomous Operation`, `Execute Timetable` and `Return Home`, and double-click a path on the Auto tab if one is offered.
| 7. Put the link back: Autonomy > Edit Autonomy on Page, right-click the same end, choose `Pair with a Link...`, pick the other end, and press `Save Changes`.
| 8. Press `Start Autonomous Operation` and let a train set off.  While autonomy runs open Locomotives > Add Locomotive.  Then right-click a locomotive in Locomotives > Browse Database and choose `Edit Name/Address/Decoder`, then `Delete from Database`.  Then open Layouts > Open Layout..., Layouts > Create New Layout and Layouts > Manage Pages > Rename Current Page (type any new name when it asks).  Press `Graceful Stop` and wait until every train has stopped.
| 9. With nothing running, no editor open and the power on, press `Start Autonomous Operation` once more, then `Graceful Stop`.  Open Locomotives > Add Locomotive and close it again.
|
| **Expected**
|
| - Step 1: every press and the double-click is refused with a window saying "Close the editor first - autonomy cannot be changed from here while it is open."  No train moves, and `Start Autonomous Operation`, `Execute Timetable` and `Return Home` are still available afterwards.
| - Step 2: with the track editor open the same sentence appears for `Start Autonomous Operation` and for the double-click, and no train moves.  Closing asks the question, and afterwards nothing of yours is kept.
| - Step 3: each of the four is refused with "The route <name> is running.  Wait for it to finish, then try again." and no train moves.  (If you ran two routes at once, the sentence reads "These routes are running: <names>.  Wait for them to finish, then try again.")
| - Step 4: editing and deleting a locomotive the route drives each say "<locomotive> is being driven by the route <route>, which is running now.  Wait for it to finish, or stop it, and try again." and change nothing.  Open Layout... and Create New Layout each say "Not while autonomy, a timetable, Return Home or a route is running.  Stop it first." and open no folder window.
| - Step 5: all four are refused with "To start autonomy, please turn the track power on, or cycle the power."  After `ON` the same presses are accepted again.
| - Step 6: `Start Autonomous Operation` is refused with either "Autonomy cannot start while the setup has <N> error(s). Open the autonomy editor to see them." or "This setup cannot be used yet: <N> things have to be dealt with first.  The count along the top of the track diagram opens the editor at the first of them, and the "Things to look at" list there says what each is and where."  `Execute Timetable`, `Return Home` and the double-click are refused with "This setup cannot be used yet: ..." (the second sentence above, or the "one thing" form).  No train moves.
| - Step 7: the setup is whole again and the banner about the setup is gone.
| - Step 8: Add Locomotive, Edit Name/Address/Decoder, Delete from Database, Open Layout..., Create New Layout and Rename Current Page each say "Cannot edit locomotives while autonomy is running." and change nothing.  Nothing is renamed, no folder window opens, and the locomotive list is unchanged.
| - Step 9: autonomy starts and stops as usual and Add Locomotive opens its window: no refusal is left over from the earlier steps.
|
| *What this is:* FR-136 Phase 5 moved the code that refuses these actions out of the main window class into `RunGates` without changing what it does.  Any difference from before is a defect of the move.

| 7. Set up a route that would switch an accessory while a train is standing at the platform that accessory protects (or while a train is running over it).  Run it from the Routes tab.  When the question comes up, press `Cancel`.  Open the Log tab.
|
| **Expected**
|
| - Step 1: the item reads "Gray Station Labels" (not "Grey"), and its tooltip says "Draw station labels in light gray instead of blue."
| - Step 2: ticking draws the station names in light gray; unticking brings back blue.
| - Step 3: the box reads `Grid`, and its tooltip says "Draw the gray grid behind the diagram, with the column and row numbers around it.  Control+K."
| - Step 4: the question reads "What should the combined page be called?" and the offered name is "<page> and neighbors", for example "Main and neighbors".  If the page has no links you get "This page has no links to other pages, so a combined page would only show this one." instead; choose another page.
| - Step 5: every page that was there before has the same name as before; only the new page carries the new name.
| - Step 6: the combined page is gone and the other pages are untouched.
| - Step 7: the question reads "The route "<route>" would switch "<accessory>", which is protecting a platform where a train is standing.  Run it anyway?" (or "...which is on track a train is running over right now.").  After Cancel the Log says "Route <route> was canceled: you declined its conflicting accessory command, so nothing further in the route was run."  The word is "canceled" with one l, and the route runs nothing.
|
| *What this is:* The program's English text now uses US spelling: "gray" for "grey", "canceled" for "cancelled", and "neighbors" for a combined page's name.  Only wording changed, nothing else.  Any other "grey", "cancelled" or "neighbours" you come across in the English text is a miss.
